title: Unramified field fibres detect the etale locus of a flat presentation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$, $q:U\to\mathcal X$ a flat locally finitely presented morphism from a scheme, and $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal X$ a map from a field. Put $F=U\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}k$. Suppose there is an etale map $V\to F$ from a scheme and $v\in V$ such that $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified at $v$, meaning unramified on an open neighbourhood of $v$. If $u$ is the image of $v$ in $U$, there exists an open neighbourhood $U_1\subset U$ of $u$ such that $U_1\to\mathcal X$ is etale. Flatness, local finite presentation, etale, unramified and open use [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-unramified-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion]. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stack, 2-fibre product and representability by algebraic spaces use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Properties of representable morphisms are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts.

source.place: Tag 06N2 (lemma-etale-at-point); its fibre hypothesis expressed on an etale scheme chart, using the etale-local definition of unramifiedness.

proof.text: The diagonal $\Delta:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ is representable by algebraic spaces. Given schemes $Z,T$ with maps $z:Z\to\mathcal X$ and $t:T\to\mathcal X$, the cited groupoid formula identifies $Z\times_{\mathcal X}T$ with $(Z\times_ST)\times_{\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X,\,(z,t)}\mathcal X$: over a test scheme, both classify pairs of maps to $Z,T$ with an isomorphism of their images; arrows satisfy the same compatibility equation. The right side is an algebraic space by representability of $\Delta$. With $Z=U$ or $Z=\operatorname{Spec}k$, this proves representability of $q$ and $a$ for every scheme test map $T\to\mathcal X$. The calculus lemma gives that $q$ is locally of finite type from local finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 06N2 (lemma-etale-at-point), cartesian diagram and base-change hypotheses

proof.text: Apply the locus lemma to the representable locally finite type map $q$, obtaining its largest unramified open $W\subset U$. Its representable base-change clause applies to $a$ by step 1 and identifies the unramified open in $F$ with $F\times_UW$. For $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the given etale map $c:V\to F$, the chart clause says that $c^{-1}(F\times_UW)$ is the union of opens of $V$ on which $V\to T$ is unramified. The assumed open neighbourhood of $v$ is such an open, hence $v\in c^{-1}(F\times_UW)$. Following the projection $F\times_UW\to W$ shows that its image $u$ lies in $W$; neither chart surjectivity nor unramifiedness at other points of $F$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 06N2, locus argument; use the unramified locus via stacks-properties.tex Tags 06M3 and 06M5(3)

proof.text: Membership of $v$ in the inverse image in step 2 means that its image $u$ lies in $W$. The locus lemma gives $q|_W$ unramified. Flatness survives restriction because the local rings at points of an open subscheme are unchanged. For local finite presentation, on each scheme chart shrink a finite-presentation affine neighbourhood to a basic open inside the inverse image of $W$. If its ring is $B=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$, that basic open has ring $B[1/b]=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n,t]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m,\widetilde b t-1)$, where $\widetilde b$ is any polynomial lifting $b$, still finitely presented. Thus $q|_W$ retains both properties on every chart.

source.place: Tag 06N2, concluding restriction to an open neighbourhood

proof.text: Set $U_1=W$. To test $U_1\to\mathcal X$ for etaleness, take any scheme base change and any etale scheme chart of its source. By the meaning of the three properties, the resulting scheme morphism is locally of finite presentation, flat and unramified. It is therefore etale by [def-weil-etale-morphism], whose defining condition is exactly this conjunction. This holds for all the charts, proving that $U_1\to\mathcal X$ is etale. Step 3 gives $u\in U_1$.

source.place: Tag 06N2, final use of spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 06LU (lemma-unramified-flat-lfp-etale); here immediate from the DAG etale definition

proof_origin.place: Tag 06N2 (lemma-etale-at-point); use the unramified open locus of Tags 06M3 and 06M5(3), which equals the etale open locus for the flat lfp morphism q.
